prompts.cover: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: literary short-story cover for The Last Watch, portrait 9:16, target 864x1536. Exact title text once: "The Last Watch", large readable cream serif lettering in the upper quarter, generous safe margins. No author name or other text. A restrained Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil painting, broad rhythmic color/value shapes, varied directional opaque brushstrokes, selective impasto and quiet connecting passages. Referenced orchard painting is only a reference for paint handling, not setting or characters. At the threshold of a humble stone watch house, an elderly woman Olla, seventy-two, grey hair, plain worn dark wool clothing, steps slowly down one shallow stone step. Her young husband Talven, about twenty-five, brown eyes, short beard, a pale scar through one eyebrow, uneven badly cropped brown hair, torn muted brown-grey coat, holds a sleeping swaddled infant against his left shoulder and lowers his right hand so Olla can take it with her left. Both faces are quiet and uncertain; age difference is unmistakable, no sentimental smile. Hands and the adjustment of their heights are the emotional focal point. Behind them in shadow are two tall rough black stones now touching with a narrow dry seam, and an empty simple wooden chair. Pale winter daylight outside, connected moss-grey and umber shadows, soft plum-brown accents, no orange-blue spectacle. Novel cover composition with stillness and negative space, not a plot montage. No glowing magical wrist bindings in this after-closure scene, no weapons, no armor, no crowns, no extra people, no graphic injury. Preserve readable title and coherent hands. Input image 1 is Talven's accepted character sheet: preserve his facial identity, haircut, scar, beard and coat, but do not copy its layout or any label except the exact cover title. At this departure he wears two oversized borrowed shoes and has no wrist loop; the infant is wrapped in a plain wool blanket. Input image 2 supplies oil brushwork only.

prompts.location: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: original location reference painting, landscape 1536x1024. The rift watch site in The Last Watch, before closure, no people and no text. Two tall rough black stones rise from a cold bare stone floor with a narrow upright dark crack between them, just wide enough for one person to squeeze through. A simple wooden chair beside each near side of the stones, one further chair opposite, a fourth weathered armchair slightly back. The site is sheltered by a modest low timber-and-stone watch house opening onto a bleak hillside, with an adjacent small resting house doorway. A folded wool blanket lies at the opposite station; a plain cup holds a letter down on a flat stone by one chair. Through the doorway the ordinary hillside and pale winter daylight; no invented city, castle, technology, canal or monumental temple. Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil painting, broad irregular rhythmic color shapes, varied directional opaque brushstrokes, selective substantial impasto, simplified grounded architecture. Ash-grey stone, brown wood, moss/umber connected shadows, muted plum and cold cream daylight. Darkness inside crack remains quiet and deep, no electric neon, runes, swirling vortex, dramatic light rays or orange-blue contrast. The referenced orchard and stream paintings guide only brushwork and value organization, not their literal scenery. Compose spatially intelligible work stations around the black stones, invitations to a fifty-year watch rather than fantasy spectacle.
